papers.name: Paper 1H (Higher Tier)
instructions: Use black ink or ball-point pen.
Fill in the boxes at the top of this page with your name, centre number and candidate number.
Correct answers without enough working may be given no marks.
Answer the questions in the spaces provided; there may be more space than you need.
Do not write on the formulae page: anything written there will not be marked.
information: The total mark for this paper is 100.
The marks for each question are shown in brackets; use them as a guide to how much time to spend on each question.
advice: Read each question carefully before you start to answer it.
Check your answers if you have time at the end.
papers.materials: You must have: ruler graduated in centimetres and millimetres, protractor, pair of compasses, pen, HB pencil, eraser, calculator. Tracing paper may be used.

sections.title: Answer ALL questions
sections.instructions: Write your answers in the spaces provided. You must write down all the stages in your working.

papers.name: Paper 2H (Higher Tier)
instructions: Use black ink or ball-point pen.
Fill in the boxes at the top of this page with your name, centre number and candidate number.
Correct answers without enough working may be given no marks.
Answer the questions in the spaces provided; there may be more space than you need.
Do not write on the formulae page: anything written there will not be marked.
information: The total mark for this paper is 100.
The marks for each question are shown in brackets; use them as a guide to how much time to spend on each question.
advice: Read each question carefully before you start to answer it.

sections.title: Answer ALL questions
sections.instructions: Write your answers in the spaces provided. You must write down all the stages in your working.

qtypes.label: Short calculation
qtypes.description: One or two steps: evaluate, simplify, write down, round, convert.

qtypes.label: Multi-step problem
qtypes.description: Unstructured problem, often in context, needing a chain of methods.

qtypes.label: Algebraic manipulation
qtypes.description: Expand, factorise, simplify, rearrange or solve, showing clear algebraic working.

qtypes.label: Show that / proof
qtypes.description: Show a given result or prove a statement, with every step or reason shown.

qtypes.label: Graph or diagram
qtypes.description: Plot, draw, read from or interpret a graph, grid or diagram.

qtypes.label: Statistics / probability data
qtypes.description: Work from a frequency table, statistical diagram, tree or Venn diagram.

qtypes.label: Structured multi-part
qtypes.description: Several linked parts (a), (b), (c) building on one context or result.

subtopics.title: Factors, multiples and primes
subtopics.summary: Prime factor form, HCF and LCM, and problems that hinge on them.

points.summary: Know the meaning of odd, even, prime, factor and multiple.
Find prime factors, common factors and common multiples.
Write a whole number as a product of prime powers.
Work out the HCF and LCM of two or three numbers.

subtopics.title: Fractions and recurring decimals
subtopics.summary: Calculate with fractions and mixed numbers; turn recurring decimals into fractions.

points.summary: Simplify fractions and recognise equivalent ones.
Switch between mixed numbers and improper fractions.
Order fractions and find a fraction of an amount.
Write one quantity as a fraction of another.
Add and subtract fractions and mixed numbers using a common denominator.
Change a fraction into a decimal or a percentage.
Multiply and divide fractions and mixed numbers.
Change a terminating decimal into a fraction or percentage.
Use algebra to change a recurring decimal into an exact fraction.

subtopics.title: Powers, roots and surds
subtopics.summary: Evaluate expressions with negative and fractional powers; simplify and rationalise surds.

points.summary: Recognise square and cube numbers.
Find squares, cubes and their roots.
Apply the index laws to whole-number powers, including zero and negatives.
Know what a surd is and simplify surds.
Expand brackets containing surds and rationalise a denominator.
Evaluate numbers raised to negative and fractional powers.

subtopics.title: Sets and Venn diagrams
subtopics.summary: Read and use set notation, complete Venn diagrams and count elements in regions.

points.summary: Know what a set is and list its members.
Use the symbols for union, intersection and membership.
Use the universal set and the empty set.
Find the complement of a set.
Show sets on a Venn diagram.
Work with sets described by a rule and with subsets.
Use Venn diagrams to show how many elements are in each region.
Use n(A) to mean the number of elements of A.
Solve practical problems with sets, including unknown regions.

subtopics.title: Percentages
subtopics.summary: Percentage change, reverse percentages, compound interest, depreciation and repeated change.

points.summary: Write one amount as a percentage of another.
Use multipliers to find percentages of amounts.
Work out percentage increases, decreases and percentage change.
Find the original amount before a percentage change.
Work out compound interest and depreciation.
Combine several percentage changes into one overall change.
Solve harder compound growth and decay problems, including finding the number of years.

subtopics.title: Ratio and proportion
subtopics.summary: Simplify and share in ratios, combine ratios, best value and map scales.

points.summary: Write ratios in simplest form or as 1 : n and link them to fractions.
Share an amount in a given ratio.
Use proportional reasoning to find unknown amounts.
Scale quantities that vary in direct proportion, e.g. recipes.
Solve ratio word problems, including maps and scale drawings.

subtopics.title: Rounding, estimation and bounds
subtopics.summary: Round to significant figures, estimate, and find upper and lower bounds of calculations.

points.summary: Round to a number of significant figures or decimal places.
Write down the upper and lower bounds of a rounded value.
Estimate a calculation by rounding each number to 1 significant figure.
Find the greatest or least value of a calculation from rounded measurements.

subtopics.title: Standard form
subtopics.summary: Convert to and from standard form and calculate with very large or small numbers.

points.summary: Write and interpret numbers as a × 10ⁿ and calculate with them.
Solve problems in context with numbers in standard form.

subtopics.title: Applying number: money, units and time
subtopics.summary: Currency conversion, unit conversion, time calculations and calculator work.

points.summary: Use number in everyday contexts such as bills and wages.
Convert between metric units of length, mass, area, volume and capacity.
Work with time, money and exchange rates.
Use a calculator efficiently and give answers to a sensible accuracy.

subtopics.title: Indices in algebra
subtopics.summary: Simplify algebraic terms using index laws, including zero, negative and fractional powers.

points.summary: Write repeated multiplication with powers.
Apply the index laws to simple algebraic terms.
Use fractional, negative and zero indices in algebra.

subtopics.title: Expanding and factorising
subtopics.summary: Expand single, double and triple brackets; factorise including quadratics with a leading coefficient.

points.summary: Collect like terms.
Multiply a term over a bracket.
Take out common factors.
Expand two linear brackets.
Factorise quadratics of the form x² + bx + c.
Expand three or more linear brackets.
Factorise quadratics including ax² + bx + c and the difference of two squares.

subtopics.title: Algebraic fractions
subtopics.summary: Simplify, add, subtract, multiply and divide algebraic fractions, and solve equations with them.

points.summary: Manipulate algebraic fractions with numeric, linear or quadratic parts.

subtopics.title: Completing the square
subtopics.summary: Rewrite quadratics in completed-square form and use it to find turning points.

points.summary: Write a quadratic in the form a(x + b)² + c.

subtopics.title: Algebraic proof
subtopics.summary: Use algebra to prove statements about numbers and identities.

points.summary: Build algebraic arguments and proofs, e.g. about odd, even and consecutive numbers.

subtopics.title: Formulae and changing the subject
subtopics.summary: Substitute into formulae and rearrange, including when the subject appears twice or is squared.

points.summary: Substitute positive, negative and fractional values into formulae.
Write a formula or expression from a description.
Rearrange a formula where the subject appears once.
Rearrange formulae where the subject appears twice or under a power or root.

subtopics.title: Linear equations
subtopics.summary: Solve linear equations including brackets and fractions, and set them up from contexts.

points.summary: Solve linear equations with the unknown on one or both sides, including fractions.
Form a linear equation from information and solve it.

subtopics.title: Direct and inverse proportion
subtopics.summary: Form and use equations for y proportional or inversely proportional to x, x², x³ or √x.

points.summary: Set up proportion equations, find the constant and use them; link them to graphs.

subtopics.title: Simultaneous linear equations
subtopics.summary: Solve two linear equations together, including from a context, and link to graphs.

points.summary: Solve a pair of simple simultaneous linear equations.
Find exact solutions of two linear simultaneous equations.
See the solution as the point where two lines cross.

subtopics.title: Quadratic equations
subtopics.summary: Solve quadratics by factorising, by the formula or by completing the square, including from contexts.

points.summary: Solve x² + bx + c = 0 by factorising.
Solve quadratics with any leading coefficient by factorising.
Use the quadratic formula or completing the square.
Form a quadratic equation from a context and solve it.

subtopics.title: Linear and quadratic simultaneous equations
subtopics.summary: Solve a linear equation together with a quadratic or circle equation.

points.summary: Solve simultaneous equations where one is linear and one is quadratic.

subtopics.title: Inequalities
subtopics.summary: Solve linear and quadratic inequalities and describe or shade regions on a graph.

points.summary: Use inequality symbols, including double inequalities.
Show inequalities on a number line with open and closed circles.
Solve linear inequalities and list integer solutions.
Identify regions on a grid from simple inequalities.
Solve quadratic inequalities.
Find inequalities that define a region bounded by several lines.

subtopics.title: Sequences and arithmetic series
subtopics.summary: Find and use nth terms, and the sum of an arithmetic series.

points.summary: Generate terms from term-to-term or position-to-term rules.
Find the nth term of a linear sequence.
Use the first term a and common difference d of an arithmetic sequence.
Use the nth term formula a + (n − 1)d.
Find the sum of the first n terms of an arithmetic series.

subtopics.title: Function notation, composite and inverse functions
subtopics.summary: Evaluate functions, find composite and inverse functions and excluded values.

points.summary: Think of a function as a rule that maps inputs to outputs.
Use the notation f(x) and f : x ↦ ….
Know what domain and range mean and which inputs must be excluded.
Find composite functions fg(x) and inverse functions f⁻¹(x).

subtopics.title: Straight-line graphs
subtopics.summary: Gradients, intercepts, midpoints and equations of lines, including parallel and perpendicular lines.

points.summary: Find the midpoint of a line segment.
Find the gradient of a line.
Use y = mx + c to read gradient and intercept.
Find gradients and equations of lines through two points.
Find equations of lines parallel or perpendicular to a given line.

subtopics.title: Plotting and using graphs of functions
subtopics.summary: Complete tables, plot quadratic, cubic and reciprocal graphs and use them to solve equations.

points.summary: Plot linear and quadratic graphs from a table of values.
Plot and recognise cubic, reciprocal and trigonometric graphs.
Estimate the gradient of a curve by drawing a tangent.
Use intersections of a line and a curve to solve equations.

subtopics.title: Real-life graphs
subtopics.summary: Read and draw distance-time, speed-time and conversion graphs.

points.summary: Interpret linear and non-linear graphs in context, including travel graphs.
Draw and use straight-line conversion graphs.
Understand rate of change, e.g. a gradient as a speed or acceleration.

subtopics.title: Transformations of graphs
subtopics.summary: Translate and stretch graphs of y = f(x) and write the new function.

points.summary: Apply f(x) + a, f(x + a), af(x) and f(ax) to graphs.
Describe a graph transformation and write the new function algebraically.

subtopics.title: Differentiation
subtopics.summary: Differentiate powers of x, find gradients and turning points, and apply to motion.

points.summary: Differentiate integer powers of x.
Use dy/dx for gradients, rates of change and turning points.
Decide whether a turning point is a maximum or minimum.
Use differentiation for velocity, acceleration and simple optimisation.

subtopics.title: Angles, triangles and polygons
subtopics.summary: Angle facts, parallel lines, triangle and polygon angles with geometric reasons.

points.summary: Use angles on a line, at a point, vertically opposite and with parallel lines.
Use the angle sum and exterior angle of a triangle.
Use properties of isosceles, equilateral and right-angled triangles.
Use the angle sum of a quadrilateral.
Find interior and exterior angles of regular polygons.
Use the angle sum of any polygon.
Give standard geometric reasons for each angle found.

subtopics.title: Compound measures and bearings
subtopics.summary: Speed, density, pressure, rates and three-figure bearings.

points.summary: Use three-figure bearings.
Use speed = distance ÷ time.
Use compound measures such as density and pressure.

subtopics.title: Constructions, loci and scale drawings
subtopics.summary: Ruler-and-compass constructions, loci and scale drawings with bearings.

points.summary: Construct triangles accurately.
Solve problems with scale drawings.
Construct perpendicular bisectors and angle bisectors with compasses.
Use maps and scale drawings.

subtopics.title: Circle theorems
subtopics.summary: Use tangent, chord and angle properties of circles, giving reasons.

points.summary: Use tangent and chord properties, e.g. tangent meets radius at 90°.
Use the intersecting chords properties.
Recognise a cyclic quadrilateral.
Use the circle angle theorems, including the alternate segment theorem.
Give standard geometric reasons for each angle found.

subtopics.title: Pythagoras and right-angled trigonometry
subtopics.summary: Find sides and angles in right-angled triangles, including elevation and bearings.

points.summary: Use Pythagoras' theorem in two dimensions.
Use sin, cos and tan to find sides and angles of right-angled triangles.
Apply trigonometry to problems in two dimensions, including bearings.
Use angles of elevation and depression.

subtopics.title: Sine rule, cosine rule and area of a triangle
subtopics.summary: Solve any triangle with the sine and cosine rules and use ½ab sin C.

points.summary: Use sine, cosine and tangent of obtuse angles.
Use the sine rule and cosine rule in any triangle.
Find the area of a triangle using ½ab sin C.

subtopics.title: Trigonometry in three dimensions
subtopics.summary: Pythagoras and trigonometry in cuboids, prisms and pyramids, including line-plane angles.

points.summary: Use Pythagoras' theorem in three dimensions.
Find lengths and angles in 3D, including the angle between a line and a plane.

subtopics.title: Perimeter, area, arcs and sectors
subtopics.summary: Areas of triangles, trapezia and circles; arc lengths and sector areas.

points.summary: Convert area units within the metric system.
Find areas of parallelograms and trapezia.
Find circumferences and areas of circles and semicircles.
Find arc lengths, sector perimeters and sector areas.

subtopics.title: Volume and surface area
subtopics.summary: Volumes and surface areas of prisms, cylinders, cones, spheres and composite solids.

points.summary: Find the surface area of a cylinder.
Find volumes of prisms, cuboids and cylinders.
Convert between units of volume and capacity.
Find surface areas and volumes of spheres and cones.

subtopics.title: Similar shapes
subtopics.summary: Use length, area and volume scale factors for similar shapes and solids.

points.summary: Use the fact that similar shapes have sides in the same ratio.
Use area scale factor = (length scale factor)².
Use volume scale factor = (length scale factor)³.
Solve problems with areas and volumes of similar shapes.

subtopics.title: Vectors
subtopics.summary: Column vectors, magnitude, vector paths and simple vector proofs.

points.summary: Use column vectors and vector notation.
Multiply a vector by a scalar.
Add and subtract vectors.
Find the magnitude of a vector.
Find a resultant vector along a path.
Use vectors to prove geometric results such as parallel lines.

subtopics.title: Transformations
subtopics.summary: Reflect, rotate, translate and enlarge shapes on a grid and describe transformations fully.

points.summary: Rotate a shape about a point.
Reflect a shape in a given line.
Translate a shape using a column vector.
Enlarge a shape by a positive or fractional scale factor.
Describe a single transformation completely.

subtopics.title: Averages and grouped data
subtopics.summary: Mean, median, mode and range from lists and tables, including estimates from grouped data.

points.summary: Understand what an average represents.
Find mean, median, mode and range, and solve problems with them.
Estimate the mean from a grouped frequency table.
Identify the modal class.

subtopics.title: Histograms
subtopics.summary: Draw and interpret histograms with unequal class widths using frequency density.

points.summary: Construct and interpret histograms with unequal class intervals.

subtopics.title: Cumulative frequency
subtopics.summary: Draw cumulative frequency graphs and use them for medians, quartiles and estimates.

points.summary: Draw a cumulative frequency graph from a table.
Read estimates from a cumulative frequency graph.
Estimate the median from a cumulative frequency graph.
Estimate the interquartile range from a cumulative frequency graph.

subtopics.title: Quartiles and measures of spread
subtopics.summary: Find quartiles and interquartile range from data and compare distributions.

points.summary: Understand what a measure of spread tells you.
Find the quartiles and interquartile range of a discrete data set.

subtopics.title: Probability
subtopics.summary: Probability scale, sample spaces, relative frequency, expected frequency and Venn probabilities.

points.summary: Find probabilities from a Venn diagram.
Use sample spaces to find probabilities.
Estimate probabilities from relative frequency.
Use P(not A) = 1 − P(A).
Add probabilities of mutually exclusive events.
Work out expected frequencies.

subtopics.title: Tree diagrams and combined events
subtopics.summary: Tree diagrams, independent events and conditional probability without replacement.

points.summary: Draw and use tree diagrams.
Find the probability of two or more independent events.
Use conditional probability, e.g. picking without replacement.
Apply probability to problems in context.
